_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Comoros covering Swahili-Arab sultanates, French colonisation, Mayotte separation, Bob Denard mercenary coups, and Grande Comore volcanism.

ethnic_groups.name: Comorian (Antalote, Cafre, Makoa, Oimatsaha, Sakalava)
ethnic_groups.notes: Mixed Bantu, Arab, Malagasy, and Shirazi heritage; Shikomori language with island dialects; no distinct tribal divisions as on mainland Africa

ethnic_groups.name: Makua
ethnic_groups.notes: Descendants of enslaved Mozambican peoples; concentrated on Mayotte and Anjouan

ethnic_groups.name: Arab-Shirazi
ethnic_groups.notes: Descendants of Arab and Persian traders; historically dominant aristocracy (kabaila)

ethnic_groups.name: Malagasy
ethnic_groups.notes: Sakalava and other Malagasy communities; cultural and linguistic influence

ethnic_groups.name: French
ethnic_groups.notes: Small European community, mainly on Mayotte

current_leader.name: Azali Assoumani
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: Third term (also served 1999-2006); 2018 referendum removed island rotation system

former_leaders.name: Ahmed Abdallah
former_leaders.notes: First president; restored by Denard; killed 1989

former_leaders.name: Ali Soilih
former_leaders.notes: Revolutionary socialist; radical youth reforms; overthrown and killed

former_leaders.name: Said Mohamed Djohar
former_leaders.notes: Abdallah's successor; ousted by Denard's last coup

former_leaders.name: Mohamed Taki Abdoulkarim
former_leaders.notes: Died in office during Anjouan crisis

former_leaders.name: Azali Assoumani
former_leaders.notes: First term; military coup then elected under new union constitution

910.name: Volcanic Origins and Early Settlement
910.description: Volcanic archipelago formation in the Mozambique Channel; earliest Bantu and Austronesian settlers arrive.

sub_clusters.name: Volcanic Formation of the Archipelago
sub_clusters.description: Formation of Grande Comore, Mohéli, Anjouan, and Mayotte through volcanic activity; Mount Karthala as active volcano.

sub_clusters.name: Early Bantu and Austronesian Settlers
sub_clusters.description: Bantu-speaking peoples from East Africa and possible Austronesian influence; proto-Swahili settlements.

920.name: Swahili-Arab Sultanates
920.description: Islamisation of the islands; establishment of competing sultanates; Shirazi and Arab merchant influence; integration into Indian Ocean trade networks.

sub_clusters.name: Islamisation of the Comoros
sub_clusters.description: Arrival of Arab and Shirazi traders; conversion to Islam; oldest mosques built; Islamic culture becomes dominant.

sub_clusters.name: Competing Sultanate System
sub_clusters.description: Multiple sultanates on each island; Ndzuwani (Anjouan) and Ngazidja (Grande Comore) most powerful; trade in slaves, spices, and ambergris.

sub_clusters.name: Indian Ocean Trade Networks
sub_clusters.description: Comoros as waystation between East Africa, Madagascar, Arabia, and India; cosmopolitan trading culture.

930.name: European Contact and Sultanate Decline
930.description: Portuguese sighting; Malagasy raids from Madagascar; internal sultanate warfare; gradual French interest.

sub_clusters.name: Portuguese Contact
sub_clusters.description: Portuguese navigators visit the Comoros en route to India; limited lasting impact on the islands.

sub_clusters.name: Malagasy Raids and Internal Conflicts
sub_clusters.description: Devastating Sakalava and Betsimisaraka raids from Madagascar; slave raiding; inter-sultanate warfare weakens islands.

sub_clusters.name: Early French Interest
sub_clusters.description: France acquires Mayotte from Sultan Andriantsoly 1841; beginning of colonial encroachment.

940.name: French Colonial Comoros
940.description: French protectorates then full colonisation; plantation economy (ylang-ylang, vanilla); administered from Madagascar.

sub_clusters.name: Protectorates and Annexation
sub_clusters.description: France establishes protectorates over remaining islands; full annexation 1912; Comoros attached to Madagascar colony.

sub_clusters.name: Plantation Economy
sub_clusters.description: French settlers establish ylang-ylang, vanilla, and clove plantations; forced labour; economic dependency on cash crops.

sub_clusters.name: Autonomy and Independence Movement
sub_clusters.description: Comoros become separate overseas territory 1946; Ahmed Abdallah and Said Mohamed Cheikh lead independence movement.

950.name: Independence and Mayotte Separation
950.description: Unilateral declaration of independence 1975; Mayotte votes to remain French; Ali Soilih's revolutionary regime.

sub_clusters.name: Independence Declaration
sub_clusters.description: Ahmed Abdallah declares independence 6 July 1975; three islands vote yes, Mayotte votes to stay French.

sub_clusters.name: Ali Soilih Revolutionary Regime
sub_clusters.description: Ali Soilih overthrows Abdallah; radical socialist youth revolution; destruction of civil records; anti-tradition campaigns.

sub_clusters.name: Mayotte Remains French
sub_clusters.description: Mayotte's refusal to join independent Comoros; UN resolutions affirm Comorian sovereignty but France retains control; Mayotte becomes département 2011.

950.name: Bob Denard Mercenary Coups
950.description: French mercenary Bob Denard dominates Comorian politics through serial coups; Abdallah restored then killed; instability.

sub_clusters.name: 1978 Denard Coup and Abdallah Restoration
sub_clusters.description: Bob Denard overthrows Ali Soilih; restores Ahmed Abdallah; Denard commands presidential guard; Abdallah killed 1989.

sub_clusters.name: 1995 Denard Coup Attempt
sub_clusters.description: Denard stages final coup; French military intervention restores order; Denard arrested and deported.

960.name: Island Separatism and Reconciliation
960.description: Anjouan and Mohéli secessions; African Union intervention; new union constitution; ongoing inter-island tensions.

sub_clusters.name: Anjouan and Mohéli Secessions
sub_clusters.description: Anjouan and Mohéli declare independence from Comoros 1997; OAU/AU mediation efforts.

sub_clusters.name: Union of the Comoros Constitution
sub_clusters.description: 2001 Fomboni Accords; rotating presidency between islands; autonomous island governments; continued tensions.

sub_clusters.name: African Union Intervention in Anjouan
sub_clusters.description: AU military operation removes renegade Anjouan president Mohamed Bacar; restores central authority.

sub_clusters.name: Azali Assoumani Consolidation
sub_clusters.description: Azali Assoumani returns to power; 2018 constitutional referendum removes rotation and island autonomy; authoritarian drift.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
